articles.title: GTA 5 Will Be Removed From PS Plus Just Before GTA 6 Releases, It Seems
articles.summary: One of the biggest games that PlayStation Plus subscribers can play as part of their membership is Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 5. However, the game will reportedly get yanked from the service soon, just ahead of GTA 6 's release.
body: The notice also includes a link directing people to the preorder page for GTA 6. "Whether you've yet to experience the tale of Franklin, Michael, and Trevor, or want to revisit it before Jason and Lucia's Vice City story begins, now's the time," Sony's notice said.
GTA 5 has rotated in and out of Xbox Game Pass over the years as well, and it is not currently available through the service.

GTA 6 launches on November 19, and the game's steamy launch trailer just arrived. The trailer was stuffed with exciting new details, so be sure to read up on GameSpot's 10 things we noticed from the GTA 6 launch trailer.

articles.title: GTA 6 Helps Modern Warfare 4, Actually, Activision Says
articles.summary: Rockstar's GTA 6 is releasing this November, and some believe it will blot out the sun when it comes to the impact it will have on the greater gaming market. The game could also help other titles, like Activision's Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.
body: “Well, no offense to Zelda, but [GTA and COD] are the two biggest games of the year. And more people coming in to the dashboards, more people taking the dust off their Xbox or PlayStation and playing again, is going to be more eyeballs for us overall," he told The Game Business.
His comment about Zelda is in reference to Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2, which launches on November 5. It's expected to be a huge hit, just like MW4 and GTA 6.

Another publisher, Ubisoft, is not afraid of GTA 6, either. CEO Yves Guillemot said when a big game like GTA 6 comes out, it helps everyone in the industry. One of Ubisoft's biggest games, Rainbow Six Siege, is actually planning to debut new content right around the time GTA 6 launches.

Bahl also stated that a big differentiator for Call of Duty is "spending time with friends," and he thinks this will hold true for MW4 this year even with GTA 6 coming to market just a few weeks after MW4 releases on October 23.
points: Rockstar's GTA 6 is releasing this November, and some believe it will blot out the sun when it comes to the impact it will have on the greater gaming market.
The game could also help other titles, like Activision's Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.
It's expected to be a huge hit, just like MW4 and GTA 6.
CEO Yves Guillemot said when a big game like GTA 6 comes out, it helps everyone in the industry.

articles.title: Activision Thinks GTA 6 Will Actually Help Modern Warfare 4: 'No Offense to Zelda, but [GTA and COD] Are the 2 Biggest Games of the Year'
articles.summary: Activision believes GTA 6 will benefit Call of Duty rather than hinder it, with the expectation that Modern Warfare 4 and Rockstar’s behemoth will end up the two biggest games of 2026.
body: In an interview with The Game Business, Activision chief marketing officer Tyler Bahl was asked about the prospect of GTA 6 and Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake both launching in November and creating a video game ‘Barbenheimer’ moment that might drown out Call of Duty.

However, Bahl said Call of Duty should be considered part of the conversation, insisting the increased attention on all things gaming, as well as the inevitable boost in sales of PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S that GTA 6 brings with it, will give Call of Duty a shot in the arm.

“Well, no offense to Zelda, but [GTA and COD] are the two biggest games of the year,” he said. “More people coming in to the dashboards, more people taking the dust off their Xbox or PlayStation and starting to play again, and loading up that experience, is going to be more eyeballs for us overall.

articles.title: Street Fighter Could Be In For A Rough First Round At The Box Office
articles.summary: Street Fighter is officially spin-kicking its way into theaters this week, starting with previews on Thursday and leading into the crucial opening weekend. It's the second movie based on a Capcom IP to make its way to the silver screen this year--following Zach Cregger's Resident Evil film in…
body: According to Deadline's box-office-predictions, Street Fighter is expected to take in under $70 million worldwide. Of that figure, it's estimated to open with a US box-office take in the high 30 millions on 3,500 screens, and a take in the mid-30 millions internationally.

Typically, movies need to make at least double their production budget back to be considered successful, and with Street Fighter costing $82 million to produce, it doesn't look like it'll recoup its expenses in its first weekend.

There's still a chance it could be a small hit if word of mouth drives audiences to theaters, and in terms of competition, Street Fighter has a few weeks to dominate cinemas as it'll be the biggest action film on the block--at least until the November 1 re-release of V for Vendetta, which is celebrating its 20th anniversary. The movie won't open in the potentially lucrative market of China, but internationally, the lion's share of sales is expected to come from Mexico, Brazil, the UK, Australia, and Asian markets.

articles.title: 10 Things We Noticed In The GTA 6 Launch Trailer
articles.summary: Rockstar is sticking to its trend of releasing some new GTA 6 news every Thursday it seems, and today's treat was the reveal of the launch trailer. After what feels like an eternity of waiting for anything, the launch trailer is the fourth official video look we've gotten at GTA 6, and the first…
body: The GTA 6 launch trailer is 90 seconds long exactly, and it gives us a closer look at some of the in-game action (and its new soundtrack composers ). While some of what see is pretty typical of games in the Grand Theft Auto series, there are a few surprising additions, and some things that hint toward just how deeply realistic the game is.

While an earlier trailer suggested as much, it now seems more certain that Lucia's journey in GTA 6 starts with her in prison. While working at the marina, Jason receives a call from her. While we don't know anything about the conversation that takes place after, the fact that she's still incarcerated while he's out and working tells us that he'll probably be keeping pretty close tabs on when she's getting released, especially since the two have clearly remained in contact.

articles.title: GTA 6 Launch Trailer Teases Jason's Troubled Past, a Steamy Shower Scene With Lucia, and Much More
articles.summary: Rockstar has released the launch trailer for GTA 6, which shows us brand new footage of Jason and Lucia as well as the open world. The trailer, which weighs in at 1:30, touches on Jason's troubled past, which involved leaving the army not on the best of terms.
body: Rather than showing gameplay, the launch trailer showcases cinematic action in GTA 6 as it nears its November 19 launch. As per Rockstar's partnership with Sony, the PS5 is prominent in the trailer, with the "plays best on PS5" message displayed at the start. The trailer confirms the footage was "captured on PS5."

The trailer begins with some narration from Jason. "I got in some trouble in the army," he begins. "Didn't leave on the best of terms. They don't give loans or anything to people like me." We see a bearded Jason working at Brian's Marina, buffing a boat before he receives a call from Lucia Caminos. Presumably this is the call Jason gets to pick up Lucia from prison.

We're shown what look like flashbacks to Jason's time in the army, where he appears to have been in the special forces. We see him wading through water as part of a military unit, and leaping out of a helicopter while on some sort of mission. But these scenes could easily be set in the "present," rather than the past, with Jason gearing up for, perhaps, a police operation. Either way, it explains why Jason is so handy with a gun.
points: Rockstar has released the launch trailer for GTA 6, which shows us brand new footage of Jason and Lucia as well as the open world.
The trailer, which weighs in at 1:30, touches on Jason's troubled past, which involved leaving the army not on the best of terms.

articles.title: South Park Season 29, Episode 3 Review & Recap: 'You Like That on Your Face'
articles.summary: Warning: This review contains full spoilers for South Park Season 29, Episode 3! Yeesh, that was probably the weakest new episode of South Park in several years. As is often the case in the show's lesser moments, "You Like That on Your Face" has a few amusing gags and ideas, but none of it comes…
body: This week, the series opts to turn its attention to Gen Z/Gen Alpha culture and hot-button issues like looksmaxxing and aura farming. Honestly, I was really hoping the opening scenes were meant to be a springboard to something else. Yes, aura farming is really stupid and laughable, but did we need an entire episode devoted to the practice?

In execution, "You Like That on Your Face" plays like a spiritual sequel to Season 8's "You Got F'd in the A," only with aura battles replacing the dance-offs of yore. Sadly, this episode compares very unfavorably to its predecessor. It hits too many of the same beats and doesn't really build on its ideas in a satisfying way. I don't know that "Hey, look how stupid and self-absorbed today's kids are" really makes for the greatest material.

This episode also leans way too heavily on the recurring gag of Sephora clerks squirting cream on children's faces and asking, "You like that on your face?" We get it. It's like porn, but with children. It's not particularly funny the first several times, and certainly not by the end when the twisted Sephora manager comes lumbering out of the darkness.

articles.title: MCU Star Teases a Completely New Avengers Project
articles.summary: The last time we saw Jeremy Renner in the Marvel Cinematic Universe was way back in 2021 in the remarkably charming Hawkeye. Since a second season of the show never materialized, the likelihood of Renner returning to the role of Clint Barton has dwindled dramatically.
body: Renner recently posted a photo on social media showing a set of The West Coast Avengers comic books. The California-based team first appeared in Marvel Comics in 1984 as an offshoot of the Avengers, who operated out of New York. Hawkeye is a founding member, and the team has also included Mockingbird, Wonder Man, Tigra, War Machine and Vision.

A West Coast Avengers project could offer several MCU characters the chance to return. Wonder Man debuted in the MCU just this year in a critically acclaimed series that Disney has since canceled. Paul Betany is currently playing Vision in VisionQuest. The latest incarnation of the West Coast Avengers was led by Kate Bishop, the other Hawkeye who appeared alongside Renner in 2021 played by Hailee Steinfeld. It also included America Chavez, who Xochitl Gomez played in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. It doesn't seem like we are ever actually getting a Young Avengers series, so West Coast Avengers could help fill that void.
points: The last time we saw Jeremy Renner in the Marvel Cinematic Universe was way back in 2021 in the remarkably charming Hawkeye.
Since a second season of the show never materialized, the likelihood of Renner returning to the role of Clint Barton has dwindled dramatically.
Renner recently posted a photo on social media showing a set of The West Coast Avengers comic books.

articles.title: With The Mummy 4 in Full Swing, Oded Fehr Jokes The Mummy 3 Doesn't Exist — Although John Hannah Firmly Disagrees
articles.summary: With The Mummy 4 currently shooting ahead of its October 15, 2027 release date, Oded Fehr, who reprises his role Ardeth Bay, joked that there were only two The Mummy movies released.
body: During a joint interview with John Hannah, who returns as Jonathan Carnahan in The Mummy 4, at Comic Con Holland, Fehr discussed what it feels like to once again play the all-action Ardeth Bay decades later. While talking about the experience, he dismissed the third The Mummy movie, subtitled Tomb of the Dragon Emperor — although Hannah clearly disagreed with the sentiment.
“It’s a very positive thing,” Fehr said of filming the originals. “The Mummy, The Mummy Returns — there wasn’t a third one — but the two movies were so… seriously, it was just fun.”
At this point, Hannah smirked and held three fingers up to the camera. He then mouthed, ‘There was a third movie.”

While it looks like a bit of harmless banter between co-stars, Fehr’s comment taps into the sentiment around the franchise going into The Mummy 4, which will see Brendan Fraser reprising his iconic role as Rick O'Connell alongside Rachel Weisz as Evelyn O'Connell.

articles.title: Epic Games Has 2 New Free PC Games That Are Only Available for a Limited Time
articles.summary: The Epic Games Store is offering two great free PC games this week. For a limited time, you can grab a rubber hose animation horror game and a spy-themed puzzle game.
body: Like April's Mouse: P.I. for Hire, Bad Cheese uses rubber hose animation that looks like it was plucked straight out of the 1920s. However, don't expect the charm of Steamboat Willie. Bad Cheese is a psychological horror game with some truly gross character designs. You play as a mouse spending a weekend home alone. While the rest of their family is away, they have to explore, clean, and contend with demons sharing their home. Typical mouse stuff.

Agent A is a stylish, retro-futuristic game where you're tasked with infiltrating an enemy spy's hideout, which is filled with tricky puzzles to solve. Take note of your surroundings, as the clues you need will be scattered about like in Blue Prince. Agent A has nearly 2,000 Overwhelmingly Positive player reviews on Steam.
If Bad Cheese and Agent A catch your eye, all you need to do is log in to the Epic Games Store and claim them. The games will be free until 11 a.m. EDT on Thursday, Oct. 22.

articles.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Is Officially Eligible for the 2026 Game Awards
articles.summary: With 2026’s most anticipated game, Grand Theft Auto 6, releasing so late in the year, many have wondered whether it would make the cutoff for the game industry’s biggest celebration of pomp and circumstance. We now have an answer.
body: The Game Awards updated an FAQ on its website, revealing that games must be commercially released before midnight ET Nov. 20 to qualify for awards in 2026. This date is close to last year’s cutoff of Nov. 21, 2025. To be eligible for the Player’s Voice category (the fan vote), games must ship on or before Nov. 30. GTA 6 releases at Nov. 19, so it gets in just under the wire.

Game industry insider NateTheHate recently claimed that Rockstar is sending critics review codes before the end of October, which would give judges ample time to play the game before they cast their votes. Last year, nominees for the 2025 Game Awards were announced on Nov. 17, four days before the cutoff. If Rockstar delays sending out codes because it's concerned about leaks, the judges would have very little time to decide whether it should be Game of the Year.

articles.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave gets its first wave of DLC today, and an expansion pass to include it
articles.summary: Nintendo and Intelligent Systems have released an expansion pass for Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, introducing a string of DLC additions to the tactical RPG starting today, and through into 2027.
body: The expansion pass, which can be bought on the Nintendo eShop for $34.99 / £29.99, comes in three parts. For those who buy it now, a selection of weapons are made available to use within the game. The second part of the expansion pass arrives this holiday season, and the final part arrives in 2027.
We already know a bit about what's coming in these latter DLC releases. The second portion features additional outfits for the game's cast, alongside three new allies: Aurora, Smyrnos, and Jurah.

The final segment of the pass looks to be the most substantial; introducing new stories to play, new allies, classes, and additional goodies. Those new stories make an already chunky game even larger, something that should give people a reason to go back to the RPG next year, and those yet to pick up the game, a convenient jumping-on point.

Fortune's Weave has been met with critical acclaim and sizable early sales figures. In Eurogamer's review, the game is described as "a synergy of everything that has made the series great for generations", and "a sumptuous feast of a game".
points: Nintendo and Intelligent Systems have released an expansion pass for Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, introducing a string of DLC additions to the tactical RPG starting today, and through into 2027.

articles.title: DC Boss Officially Reveals Mister Miracle Show’s Stars
articles.summary: Considering James Gunn has made Tom King one of the architects of the new DC Universe, it's no surprise that several of the writer's comic runs are being adapted for the screen.
body: In a wide-ranging interview with IGN, DC Studios co-head Peter Safran named the two actors who will serve as the show's leads. Josh Hutcherson ( The Hunger Games, plenty of internet memes ) will be the titular escape artist alongside Mackenzie Davis ( Station Eleven, Happiest Season ) as his wife, Big Barda. King, who recently served as co-creator of Lanterns, wrote all eight episodes of Mister Miracle himself, and Safran called the script "dynamite." "It's a beautiful book and the adaptation is fantastic, so we're excited about that," he said.

Other minor updates Safran gave included the reveal that early development on the Absolute Batman animated series is underway with Scott Snyder in the process of writing scripts. Safran's co-head of DC, James Gunn, hasn't chosen what his next directorial project will be, though Gunn himself has said he has already started writing something new.

articles.title: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse review - inspired by great ideas, but doomed by questionable execution
articles.summary: In my office, I have a collage of Ordnance Survey maps plastered across my wall. They're from places I've lived - Derbyshire, East London, Bournemouth, Bristol - with cycle routes, country roads, and parks highlighted and circled.
body: Perhaps that's why I love Metroidvanias so much. Really, the game is the map. Is there anything more intoxicating than pushing your palms up against the walls supposedly keeping you in and knowing that - somewhere - there's a hidden path leading to the other side? Over the years, you develop an instinct for it; you get to play against the sadistic engineers of these labyrinthine spaces. 'I see your mysterious overhang,' you say, 'and jump through your roof. I see your egregious slab of a wall, and phase through its illusion.'

And Castlevania: Belmont's Curse has all this in spades. There are so many sly nuances tucked away around the streets of Paris and within Dracula's Castle that it's like I'm instantly transported back to my pre-pubescent self, nudging the D-Pad against every wall in Castlevania: Symphony of the Night in a belligerent attempt to sniff out its secrets.
points: In my office, I have a collage of Ordnance Survey maps plastered across my wall.
They're from places I've lived - Derbyshire, East London, Bournemouth, Bristol - with cycle routes, country roads, and parks highlighted and circled.

And Castlevania: Belmont's Curse has all this in spades.

articles.title: DayZ creator Dean Hall says "our industry is rotting from its core" because of big-company "greed", aiming shots at Epic's Unreal and Unity
articles.summary: UPDATED 3.30PM BST: Dean Hall has explained more about his idea in an email exchange with Eurogamer, clarifying issues such as whether it uses or welcomes any form of generative AI, while offering some more strongly worded criticisms about Epic's Unreal engine and Unity.
body: Primarily, I wanted to clarify what Brutal's relationship was with generative AI, if any, because it's the tech topic of the moment and something both Epic and Unreal, and Unity, are all-in on. In this regard, Hall answered: "There is no generative AI inside it, no tooling or scripts for making generative AI assets. Anyone can see for themselves as the repository is public. The framework is a tool for putting a game or engine together, not for generating anything."

Hall then tackled generative AI more broadly, particularly as it relates to Unreal and Unity, and said he finds it "confusing" that both engines focus "so much effort" on it. They are human-centric workflows, as he calls them - presumably meaning designed to be easily digestible by humans. "What, specifically, is it about Unreal - which has long focused on visual scripting, blueprints, and such - that would make it good for AI work?" He asked. "If we take all the promises as true, why would a human-centric workflow without the human be better than a language-centric workflow provided to a language model?"

videos.title: It's so good (The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Hands-On Impressions)
videos.summary: Get up to $40 off Dbrand's legendary Killswitch case for the Switch 2 by visiting Thanks to Dbrand for sponsoring the video.
body: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is a stunning technical showcase from Nintendo, delivering a jaw-dropping Hyrule that is not only incredibly detailed, but thoughtfully lit to maximise both immersion and storytelling. Changes to traversal, combat and level layouts are subtle but do result in a game that feels more comfortable to play, without sanding back any of the things that made the original such a masterpiece. Ocarina was always perfect and remains so all these years later, but it seems as though Nintendo has found a few ways to make it that little bit more perfect.
